sources.entry: Vince | Self Hosted Alternative To Google Analytics

summary.one_liner: Vince is a self-hosted, single-binary web analytics server positioned as an alternative to Google Analytics and a drop-in replacement for Plausible Analytics scripts.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Vince as a self-hosted analytics tool that ships as a single executable with no runtime dependencies. It supports existing Plausible tracking scripts by pointing them at a Vince instance. Tracked items include outbound links, file downloads, 404 pages, and custom events. Dashboards are private by default, can be made public, or shared through unique links that can be password protected. It offers time period comparison and breakdowns by cities, sources, pages and devices, according to the comparison table. Automatic TLS via Let's Encrypt is built in. Setup uses an admin command to create a user and a serve command to start the server, with settings via command-line flags or environment variables.
use_cases: track outbound link and file download clicks
share analytics dashboards with password protection
run Plausible-compatible analytics without Elixir or ClickHouse
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash (MacOS and Linux installer; URL missing from README)
helm repo add vince (Helm chart; repo URL missing from README)
notable: Single binary with no runtime dependencies, unlike Plausible which needs Elixir, ClickHouse and PostgreSQL per the comparison table
Drop-in compatibility with existing Plausible Analytics tracking scripts
Built-in automatic TLS with Let's Encrypt
Unlimited sites and events, limited only by available resources
Started as a Go port of Plausible focused on self hosting
caveats: README says it is lean and covers only single-entity self hosting; not feature parity with Plausible (no funnels, multi-tenant or enterprise features)
Hosted offering not available per the comparison table
Install script and Helm repo URLs are missing from the README text
